subject: Post-demo: Crestline privacy action plan & PII handling confirmation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Thanks — quick follow-up and next steps on PII handling

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Couple quick items from our side so you have a clear artifact to share with your security and procurement teams.

Summary (short): Crestline asked about what we persist from user prompts and generated outputs, where it is stored, and how long logs/telemetry are retained. Below is a concise confirmation and proposed next steps.

What we store (default hosted behavior):
- Prompt input: ephemeral cache for inference (used to build context) — not written to long-term storage unless customer enables logging.
- Generated output: transient by default; persisted only when customer is on a paid plan that opts into retention for analytics or when enabled via API parameters.
- Request metadata: minimal telemetry (timestamp, model variant, latency buckets) used for service health and billing; does NOT include full prompt text unless logging is explicitly enabled.

Where it is stored:
- Hosted: primary storage is US-East (AWS); customers can select EU regions for EU-only residency.
- Dedicated/Private: data resides in customer VPC or on-prem depending on the deployment and KMS configuration.

Retention windows (defaults, configurable):
- Ephemeral inference cache: seconds–minutes (auto-evicted).
- Audit logs/telemetry: 90 days by default; configurable to 30/90/365 for enterprise plans.
- Persisted prompt/output logs (if enabled): customer-controlled; default 30 days for trial accounts, enterprise customers can set custom TTL via Console.

Security controls:
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated/Private and via Cloud KMS integration in Hosted (enterprise add-on).
- Access: role-based access and audit trails; SOC2 Type II in place (summary attached).
- Redaction: token-level redaction is available on request; we can apply deterministic redaction for PHI fields before storage.

Requested next steps:
1) I’ll attach a one-page dataflow and our SOC2 summary for your security team.
2) Could you confirm whether Crestline requires EU-only residency or customer-managed KMS? That will determine whether we propose Hosted EU region or a Dedicated deployment.
3) If Procurement wants a TAM call, we can loop Marissa for pricing and deployment options.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the artifacts in a separate message.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Emily — answers inline below.

> When logging is \"enabled for analytics\", is the prompt text encrypted-at-rest with customer-managed keys or with Redwood-managed keys?
- Hosted (default): encrypted-at-rest using Redwood-managed keys unless customer purchases the KMS add-on (enterprise).
- Hosted + KMS add-on or Dedicated/Private: supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault).

> For the token-level redaction you mentioned, is that applied server-side before any logs are written?
- Yes. Redaction is applied at the ingestion layer. We have hooks that run deterministic redactors (PII rules you provide) and those redactions happen before writing to persistent logs or analytics stores. Ephemeral caches still see the raw prompt for the duration of the inference call but those caches are not written to long-term storage unless logging is turned on.

Retention matrix: attaching a CSV that shows default TTLs by plan (trial/standard/enterprise) and configurable options.

Marissa — can you join a 30m procurement/deployment call tomorrow at 11am PT? Emily is US-only and KMS is likely required.

Rishi

- SOC2 doc: control family coverage and audit date (June 2026).
- Retention matrix: trial = 30d persisted logs; standard = 90d telemetry; enterprise = configurable up to 365d.

If Procurement needs a signed artifact or additional evidence (e.g., full SOC2 report or penetration test summary), we can route that through our security team under NDA.

Thanks — attaching now.
